notes.text: Marcus Foligno is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 14 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.

Jared Spurgeon is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. Jonas Brodin has taken his spot beside Quinn Hughes. That pair has had 40% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 73:15 together, down from 69% with Spurgeon.

Brock Faber is on injured reserve (skull surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-pair defenseman. Jonas Brodin has taken his spot beside Quinn Hughes. That pair has had 60% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 178:41 together.
Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson.
John Tavares is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Max Domi is on long-term injured reserve and has not played this season.
Dakota Mermis was added to the roster on Oct 24 and has played beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 17 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Wild go in first in the Central with 27 points, the Maple Leafs seventh in the Atlantic with 18 points.

TOR.head: The Maple Leafs face a real test
TOR.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs can pull it off if they keep dangerous shots away.

MIN.head: The Wild have a lot going for them
MIN.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: Tilted ice, toward the Maple Leafs’ net
paras: The Maple Leafs (8-7-2) lost 3-2 to Utah on Nov 3, while the Wild have won three straight. Going in, the Wild are first in the Central (second in the NHL) and the Leafs seventh in the Atlantic (19th).

The Wild’s record (.750) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.673), largely thanks to their goaltending. So is the Maple Leafs’ (.529 on chances worth .478), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Wild draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (3rd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). The Maple Leafs, by contrast, take more penalties than they draw (31st). Minnesota has allowed 2.17 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take a lot of low-quality shots (31st). The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Kirill Kaprizov (16 G / 14 A / 30 P in 18 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is tied for third in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. Quinn Hughes (6 G / 19 A / 25 P in 18 GP) is next in line, with nine points in his last five games. Auston Matthews (11 G / 15 A / 26 P in 17 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is tied for sixth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. William Nylander (10 G / 11 A / 21 P in 17 GP) is next in line.

Jesper Wallstedt (11-2-3 / .922 SV% in 16 GS) has been a rock in net for Minnesota and will likely start. Toronto has two options in net: Sergei Bobrovsky (3-6-2 / .889 SV% in 11 GS) and Anthony Stolarz (5-1-0 / .910 SV% in 6 GS). Bobrovsky has started seven of their last ten games, including the last one on Nov 3, so Toronto could turn to Stolarz to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
The Wild usually control more of the chances than the Maple Leafs do.

items.text: The Wild have been without Marcus Foligno and Jared Spurgeon for several games, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
The Maple Leafs are newly without Kirill Marchenko, have been without Nick Blankenburg and John Tavares for several games, and have had to make do without Max Domi all season.
Joel Eriksson Ek has five goals on chances worth about 9.8 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Kirill Kaprizov, Quinn Hughes, Matt Boldy and Joel Eriksson Ek have a point in seven straight games.
